taxonomyNote: NatureServe recognizes six subspecies and notes Apalone was split from Trionyx; Animal Diversity Web still lists the older name Trionyx spiniferus.
fieldMarks: Soft, flat, leathery shell without scutes, olive to tan with black speckles; flexible edge bears small spines
Narrow head ending in a tubular nose
Two light black-bordered bands on each side of the head
Males 12.7-24 cm, females larger at 24-48 cm and mottled grey
behavior: Basks on shores or partly submerged logs; buries in bottom sediment when inactive
Activity mainly April/May to October in the north; some nocturnal activity in summer
In Vermont-Québec waters moved about 3 km between wintering and nesting sites
Eats crayfish, insects, mollusks, fish and amphibians
habitat: Large rivers, impoundments, lakes and pools with open sandy or mud banks and soft bottoms.
range: Montana to southern Québec, south to northern Mexico and the Florida panhandle, with introductions elsewhere. In Québec it is concentrated around Lake Champlain and its tributaries.
